title: Flux USD Assembler Recipe
description: Authoring form of an assembly recipe. Only pipeline identities (asset+version), never absolute paths.

kind.description:
What USD entity this recipe builds, and the USD Kind it is stamped with. USD model hierarchy: assembly > group > component > subcomponent. A model root (assembly/component) is referenceable and versioned as a whole; a group is pure organisation and is never referenced on its own.
- component (USD kind=component): a single LEAF asset, whatever it is: a CHAR, a rock, a single car wheel, one prop, one env piece. Payload geometry + variant sets (lod/look/purpose). Cannot nest other models. v2 layered publishes stack per-asset slots over the geometry base (see $defs.layerKind).
- assembly (USD kind=assembly): an AGGREGATE that references several components/sub-assemblies as ONE reusable, versioned unit: all the parts of a car (body + 4 wheels + doors), all the elements of a forest, or a crowd of many characters. Use only when the group is reused as a block; independent hero CHARs go straight into the shot as components, not wrapped in an assembly.
- shot (USD kind=group): NOT a model. A container that REFERENCES (never copies) one assembly (the set) + components (the CHARs) and only authors their placement (xform) + per-dept overrides. The CHAR lives in the shot as a reference to its published CHAR_hero.usda, so on disk the shot stays a tiny file; USD composes shot + CHAR + set into ONE stage at open time, but they remain separate .usd files. Department layers stack strong->weak (lighting > fx > anim > layout); placement is authored in the weakest layer (layout).
- sequence (USD kind=group): NOT a model. Groups shots and carries the shared base light rig every shot inherits and can override.

assembly.description: The single assembly (USD kind=assembly) referenced at the root of a shot: an aggregate that groups several components as one versioned unit (all elements of a forest, all parts of a car, a crowd). It is REFERENCED, not copied; its internal dressing is authored in its own published layer, never here.

departments.description: Shot department layers, weak->strong (default: layout, anim, fx, lighting). Each becomes a sublayer of the shot root; 'lighting' is the shot light rig that overrides the sequence base rig. The composer publishes them strong->weak in subLayerPaths.

components.description: Components (USD kind=component) REFERENCED and PLACED as instances inside a shot: a CHAR, a rock, a standalone prop, each with its own xform. The shot points at the published component USD (e.g. CHAR_hero.usda) and only authors placement + per-dept overrides, never a copy of the geometry. These go directly in the shot (not wrapped in an assembly) so every one can be animated/placed per shot.

layerKind.description:
A per-asset USD slot in a v2 layered component publish. Slots sublayer strong->weak over the geometry base (stack order: anim > cam > light > shading > skel > model). These are the asset's OWN layers, not the scene: 'light' here is a light bound to the asset itself (e.g. a lamp prop's emission), NOT the shot/sequence light rig, which lives in the shot 'lighting' department and the seq/shot *_light.usda templates.
- model: geometry base (weakest).
- skel: SkelRoot + joints + skin weights.
- shading: materials/looks bound over the geometry.
- light: UsdLux lights owned by the asset, under /<asset>/.../Lighting.
- cam: a camera owned by the asset (e.g. a rig cam).
- anim: SkelAnimation / animated overrides (strongest).
